author: Bechstein, 1793
habitat: 바닷가 섬의 숲과 나무, 도시 공원의 숲
summary: 유럽에서 번식하고 아프리카에서 겨울을 나는 솔새로, 우리나라에서는 2007년 9월 독도에서 처음 사진으로 기록된 뒤 2009년 4월 가거도, 2021년 10월 서울 등에서 몇 차례만 기록된 길잃은새다. 번식지에서는 키 큰 활엽수가 들어선 숲에 살며, 나무 위쪽에서 곤충을 잡아먹고 둥지는 숲 바닥의 덤불 속에 짓는다. 서유럽에서 러시아 남서부까지 번식하고 적도 부근 서아프리카에서 겨울을 나며, 일본과 중국 동부에도 드물게 길을 잃고 찾아온다.

points.en: bright yellow throat and upper breast against a white belly

young: 어린새는 어른새와 비슷하나 윗면이 더 칙칙하고 회갈색 기운이 돌며, 멱과 가슴의 노란색이 옅다.

similar.how: 연노랑솔새는 조금 작고 날개끝이 짧으며, 노랑가슴솔새처럼 노란 멱·윗가슴과 순백색 배가 뚜렷하게 나뉘지 않는다.

art.subject: Wood Warbler (Phylloscopus sibilatrix), adult in spring: bright moss-green upperparts from crown to tail; a long, bright lemon-yellow supercilium and a dark green eye-stripe; cheeks, chin, throat and upper breast bright lemon-yellow, cut off sharply from the pure white lower breast, belly and undertail coverts; wing and tail feathers dark with bright yellow-green edges, the tertials blackish with neat pale yellowish-green fringes; bill brownish with a pale pinkish-yellow base to the lower mandible; dark eye; pale yellowish-brown legs.
art.pose: perched on a branch in the lower canopy, side view, wings slightly drooped
art.scene: deciduous broadleaf woodland on a Korean offshore island in May, fresh green leaves and dappled sunlight; no people, buildings or text
views: adult, spring, side view perched on a branch in the lower canopy: slim, fairly large leaf warbler with long wings and a fairly short tail, green upperparts, bright yellow supercilium, bright yellow throat and upper breast sharply set off from the silvery-white belly and undertail, fine pointed bill, wings slightly drooped

adult, front view perched: green crown, bright yellow supercilium and cheeks, bright yellow throat and upper breast cut off from the clean silvery-white lower breast and belly, green wings at the sides
art.build: A fairly large leaf warbler, smaller than a sparrow but noticeably larger and longer-winged than a Yellow-browed Warbler; slim and elongated, with a short tail. Bill fine and straight, shorter than the head. Legs slender, pale yellowish-brown. Very long wings: at rest the primary projection is about as long as the tertials, and the wingtips reach well down the short tail. Tail short, plain, slightly notched. Often droops and quivers its wings while singing.
avoid: Do not paint yellow on the belly; the yellow stops on the upper breast and the belly is pure white.
Do not add wing-bars (Arctic Warbler, Two-barred Warbler).
Do not paint dull brownish-grey upperparts; they are bright moss-green.
Do not give it a long tail; the wings are long and the tail short.
